verdict.rationale: Railway's own docs say its built-in agent can "set variables, connect databases, wire up networking," and that private connections are live from the moment you deploy. That suggests first-party wiring of services to databases with little manual setup. However, nothing documents a native binding model (e.g., auto-injected connection references) for databases, external APIs, or storage, so depth is unproven. Missing for 10: a documented native binding or variable-reference mechanism, any coverage of storage/object buckets or external API bindings, evidence that credentials are injected without SDK boilerplate, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can connect my code to external services like databases, APIs, and storage through native bindings with minimal boilerplate instead of hand-wiring SDKs and credentials

citations.quote: Create services, set variables, connect databases, wire up networking, and adjust resource limits.
Private connections, public endpoints, SSL, and load balancing live from the moment you deploy.
Connect your repo, Railway handles the rest. Auto-config, instant previews, no new tools to learn.
